newsitem.title: NIGERIA: British man happy to be out of Nigerian jail.
newsitem.headline: British man happy to be out of Nigerian jail.

text.p: A British man set free on Friday after two months of detention in Nigeria without charge said he was happy to be released.
"During my detention, I was fairly treated and I am now delighted to be free," said Bruce Henderson in a statement he read to reporters at the British high commission (embassy) in Lagos.

Henderson, 42, was detained on December 22 while travelling in the politically sensitive Bakassi peninsula in southeast Nigeria where troops from Nigeria and Cameroon have clashed over their rival territorial claims to the oil-rich area.
Henderson, from Aberdeenshire in Scotland, was working on a rain forest project in Cameroon.
Nigeria's former colonial power Britain strongly protested against his detention before eventually securing his release.
"I am grateful to those who helped to sustain me during this difficult time and who have worked hard to secure my release," Henderson said.
He said he had spoken to his wife and family in Britain and was looking forward to rejoining them.
A British High Commission spokesman said Henderson would leave Lagos on Friday night on a British Airways scheduled flight that will arrive at Gatwick airport early on Saturday.

Asked if the Briton had been well treated in detention the High Commission spokesman said: "He didn't have access to fresh clothes because what you see him wearing is what he was wearing when he was detained but he did have access to food."
There has been no comment from the Nigerian authorities on the detention.
